pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Toolbar.tsx:122 The /ledger read model filters on indexed actor/type/subject/time columns, pages by keyset, and labels a partial text scan as partial, so a capped or filtered result never reads as the whole population.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Toolbar.tsx:122 A capped scan says so on the surface. Facets are kernel counts that leave out their own filter, a lone id is answered by indexed subject and run lookups, and the empty state tells 'nothing recorded yet' (List.tsx:117) apart from '0 events' under a filter.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Detail.tsx:103 The detail labels whether the effective time was recorded or derived, and fieldsOf shows the ledger's own `recorded` instant beside it. The from/to window runs on coalesce(occurredAt, at), and the UI does not name that clock. That is a weak spot, but it is not judged a deviation here.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts:28 The screen's only server actions are two reads (olderEvents, relatedEvents), so it exposes no way to change a record.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Toolbar.tsx:127 When the projection sync that feeds the ledger fails, the failure shows on the query surface itself, so an empty or thin result is not passed off as complete.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:55 Events are never invalidated (append-only with seq), so there is no record-axis interval to rewind. The technique's own exemption covers this.

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/slots/schema.ts:78 The publications and metric_snapshots ledgers are append-only with no stated horizon or reaper anywhere (the search over the kernel's slots and records modules, lib/publish and workers found none), so metric readings written on a timer grow without bound, against retention-and-partitioning.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/slots/schema.ts:78 An append-only ledger with no age or count horizon at its insert door and no named reaper.

packages/kernel/src/slots/schema.ts:67 Publications and readings refuse UPDATE and DELETE at the schema, and slots refuse DELETE (cancel is soft). State rows that do mutate (runs, projects) record the change as a new event with from/to, for example launch.ts:277 run.relaunched.

packages/kernel/src/slots/write.ts:38 Every slot INSERT and UPDATE goes through one door that appends its event in the same transaction. A grep shows the record and slot tables are written only from schema.ts, write.ts, outcome.ts and import.ts, so the writers can be listed.
packages/kernel/src/slots/write.ts:61 The event carries references (ids, state, channel, rev), not the slot's free-form title, description or tags.
packages/kernel/src/slots/outcome.ts:50 The publication row doubles as the duplicate guard, so it fails the action (claim exception), and the claim is fenced by a lease (assertFence).
packages/kernel/src/slots/outcome.ts:118 The reading's own time (snap.at, stored in metric_snapshots.at) is kept apart from the ledger's recorded `at`.
